title: Knee Braces, Walking Sticks and Shoes for Arthritis: What Actually Helps?
metaDescription: Do knee braces, knee caps, walking sticks and cushioned shoes help arthritis? How to use a stick correctly and when a brace is worthwhile.
intro: A walking stick is the aid with the clearest benefit for knee arthritis. Braces, knee caps and insoles help some people but are not for everyone, and UK guidance says they are not routinely needed unless the knee feels unstable or is bowed. Choose them for a reason, not by default.

sections.heading: Does a walking stick help?
sections.body: Yes. NICE says to consider walking aids such as sticks for arthritis in the leg. A stick shares the load with your arm and takes pressure off the sore knee, which can make walking easier and safer.

sections.heading: Which hand should I hold the stick in?
sections.body: The NHS advises holding it on the side opposite your affected leg. If your right knee hurts, hold the stick in your left hand, and move the stick and the sore leg forward together.

sections.heading: Do knee braces and knee caps help?
sections.body: NICE does not routinely recommend braces, tape, splints or supports unless the knee is unstable or loaded unevenly. The NHS says leg braces and insoles can reduce pressure for some people. A physiotherapist or doctor can judge if you are one of them.

sections.heading: What shoes help?
sections.body: Shock-absorbing shoes with good cushioning can help, says the NHS. Avoid worn-out footwear and very high heels. Insoles may help some people, but they are not needed for everybody.

sections.heading: What about elastic knee caps and heat belts?
sections.body: They may feel comforting, but they do not repair the knee. If they help your pain and are comfortable, there is no harm in using them, as long as you keep exercising.

faqs.q: Is a knee brace good for arthritis?
faqs.a: It can help if your knee gives way or is bowed, but is not routinely needed.

faqs.q: Should I use a stick all the time?
faqs.a: Use it when walking is painful or on uneven ground. Your physiotherapist can advise.

faqs.q: Which shoes are good for knee arthritis?

faqs.a: Not usually. Ask us if you have a bow-leg or foot problem.
